newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt says loses trust in Israeli peace talk.
newsitem.headline: Egypt says loses trust in Israeli peace talk.

text.p: Egypt said on Tuesday it had lost its trust in any Israeli government talk about peace now that Israel has started work on a new Jewish settlement at Jabal Abu Ghneim in Arab East Jerusalem.
Foreign Minister Amr Moussa described the situation as "extremely grave" and said Israel was shortsighted if it thought Arabs would take such challenges lying down.

"I don't think that any credibility remains to the Israeli position or to any Israeli position that talks of peace, after (Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu has embarked on these measures," the minister said.
Moussa, speaking at a joint news conference with visiting Belgian Foreign Minister Erik Derycke, said the start of work on the settlement on Tuesday was also destructive to Middle East peace talks.

"Israel bears responsibility for this dangerous violation of the principles of the peace process... Egypt's position is well known -- that these Israeli measures are completely unacceptable," he added.

"Contacts will take place with Arab countries to deal with the deteriorating situation created by the Israeli position. The situation is extremely grave and destroying the peace process in this way will have dire effects," he said.

Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak and King Hussein of Jordan had tried to dissuade Netanyahu from going ahead with the settlement, where Israel is building 6,500 homes for Jews. The Israelis call the area Har Homa.

Asked what he thought of Netanyahu's defiance of Arab opinion, Moussa said: "This shortsightedness on the part of Israel because the results will not be submission or surrender. If Netanyahu thinks it will lead to Arab submission, then he is making a great mistake."
The Belgian minister said the start of work on the settlement was unfortunate and would not help build peace.
"I want to make it clear that the Arabs can rely on the European Union... to try to concentrate more on the peace process and to do all we can to save it," he added.
